_templatePurpose: QuizMaster question set for BCATS Skill Standard 40540 (v1), reorganised to separate learner self-reflection from direct assessment-workbook evidence and photo evidence.
_assessmentIntegrityNotes: The formal assessment evidence section mirrors the supplied Being safe assessment resource: identify hazards and controls, work safely, keep the workplace safe, and complete the learner evidence checklist.

Ten connected hazard-record spaces are provided as a PHS scaffold. The official assessment schedule does not set a minimum number of hazards and controls; it requires sufficient coverage of the tasks, hazards and controls needed for the project.
The learner self-reflection section contains supporting safety-learning questions that are not direct written prompts from the supplied assessment workbook.

Project Process Evidence is repeatable: learners add as many project-stage records as needed to cover all important stages. Each stage can use a photo or a written record, so a mixed evidence approach is supported.
Workplace/storage before and after tidy-up remain separate photo evidence requirements.
Teacher sign-off is intentionally omitted in this version, as requested.

questionSet.label: SS 40540 - BCATS Safety
questionSet.title: Use safety practices for a BCATS project or related tasks

assessments.title: Learner Self-reflection - Safety Knowledge
assessments.subtitle: Reflection questions that support learning but are not direct written prompts from the SS 40540 assessment workbook

questionGroups.label: Learner self-reflection
questionGroups.title: Reflect on what you learned about working safely
questionGroups.intro: These questions help you explain what you learned and how it connected to your own project. They are separate from the formal workbook evidence questions.
questionGroups.reminder: Use real examples from your own project wherever you can.

questions.text: In your own words, what is a hazard? Give one example from your BCATS project.
questions.hint: Think about something or a situation that could cause harm.

questions.text: What different types of hazards did you notice during your project? Give examples from your own work.
questions.hint: You could think about the work area, physical hazards, and the way people work.

questions.text: Before starting a task, what did you do to identify hazards and decide whether it was safe to begin?
questions.hint: Describe what you checked before starting work.

questions.text: How could a quick 'Take 5' or step-back check help you when returning to work after a break?
questions.hint: Think about what may have changed while you were away.

questions.text: Which safety signs or safety colours did you see in your work area, and what did they tell you to do?
questions.hint: Use examples you actually saw where possible.

questions.text: When you found a hazard, how did you decide whether to remove it, reduce it, or use another control? Give one example.
questions.hint: Explain the action you took and why.

questions.text: What did you do before using a tool, machine, or piece of equipment you had not used before?
questions.hint: Think about instruction, demonstration, supervision, and showing you could use it safely.

questions.text: Why is PPE important, and why should PPE not be the only safety control you rely on?
questions.hint: Think about what PPE protects and what other controls can reduce risk.

questions.text: Describe one situation in your project where noise could be a hazard. What did you do to reduce the risk to your hearing and to other people?
questions.hint: Include both hearing protection and any other control you used.

questions.text: Describe one situation where eye protection was needed. What eye protection did you use and what was the hazard?
questions.hint: Link the PPE to the actual task or hazard.

questions.text: If you had to move a heavy or awkward item, how did you make the task safer?
questions.hint: Think about planning, body position, getting help, equipment, and the route.

questions.text: What responsibilities did you have for your own safety and the safety of others while working in the BCATS area?
questions.hint: Use examples from your own project work.

questions.text: How can a hazard register or shared safety information help you work more safely in a BCATS workplace?
questions.hint: Think about knowing the hazards, controls, and who is responsible.

questions.hint: Match each item of PPE to the task or hazard it was used for.

questions.text: What other controls did you use for project-related hazards apart from PPE?
questions.hint: Examples could include guards, extraction, warnings, keeping others clear, barriers, ventilation, or changing how a task was done.

questions.text: For the project-stage photos you submitted, identify the task or stage shown and explain what PPE and other safety controls can be seen in the photo.
questions.hint: Use this answer to connect your photo evidence to the safe work you carried out.

questions.text: How did you tidy the workplace during your work and after you finished?
questions.hint: Think about benches, floors, walkways, offcuts, rubbish, tools, cords, and storage.

questions.text: What does your BEFORE tidy-up photo show? Identify the work area or storage area and what still needed to be cleaned, cleared, or put away.
questions.hint: Describe what can actually be seen in the photo.

questions.text: What does your AFTER tidy-up photo show? Explain how the photo shows the area was left tidy and tools or equipment were put away appropriately.
questions.hint: Describe what changed from the before photo.

questions.text: Record the cleaning and checks you completed on tools, equipment and PPE after use.
questions.hint: For each item, include what you cleaned or checked and what you found or did next.

questions.text: Did you find any damaged or dangerous tools or equipment? If yes, record the item, the date, the problem, and who you reported it to. If none were found, write N/A.
questions.hint: A complete report includes the item, date, issue, and the person it was reported to.

questions.text: List the main project stages covered by your submitted project-stage photos, or by your record of work if you used one instead.
questions.hint: Make sure the evidence covers the project process and identifies the safety procedures used.

questions.text: What date did you finish collecting all the evidence for this assessment?
questions.hint: Use the date when your written work and practical evidence were complete.

questions.text: What project instructions have you included in your overall portfolio of evidence?
questions.hint: Identify the instructions for the same project named at the start of this assessment.
